reviewPolicy.sourcePolicy: Keep general Element 58 valid range and card-brand-specific representation limits separate. Do not infer amount arithmetic from a range-only test.
reviewPolicy.dataPolicy: Synthetic field-level amount designs only. Product/transaction context, currency, decimal interpretation, and complete request fields require review.
reviewPolicy.baselinePolicy: References the Segment 100 Element 58 source rule and existing net-amount rule; no official Test record is modified.
reviewPolicy.promotionGate: Authorized Test review must confirm the applicable card brand, amount interpretation, full Segment 100 fixture, and expected numeric validation before promotion or execution.

requirementReferences.title: Nonfuel Amount (Element 58) is numeric with valid values 1-99999999; representation is limited to eight digits for American Express and seven digits for other card types.
Nonfuel Amount follows the net nonfuel amount rule

sourceEvidence.quote: Number: 58 Name: Nonfuel Amount Character Type: N Maximum Length: 8 bytes
sourceEvidence.interpretation: Element 58 is numeric with a global maximum of eight bytes.

sourceEvidence.quote: Variable length of up to eight digits with two assumed decimal places
sourceEvidence.interpretation: Element 58 uses two assumed decimal places; amount calculations remain outside this range draft.

sourceEvidence.quote: A maximum length of 8 bytes is allowed for American Express cards only. A maximum length of 7 bytes is allowed for all other card types.
sourceEvidence.interpretation: The eight-digit representation is card-brand-specific; non-Amex context must be limited to seven digits.
The source's general valid-value range begins at 1 and ends at 99999999, subject to the card-specific representation limits above.

aiReviewReferences.assessment: All six hash-verified candidate observations declare Segment 100 Element 58 omitted. They do not demonstrate range, numeric type, card-brand-specific width, or net amount semantics.

testScenarios.intent: In an authorized American Express Segment 100 context, probe a valid seven-digit amount, the eight-digit maximum, and an overlength value.
In an authorized non-American-Express Segment 100 context, probe the seven-digit maximum and an eight-digit value that exceeds the card-specific width.

testCases.assertion: A numeric eight-digit Element 58 value is within the documented Amex width and general value ceiling.
A nine-digit Element 58 value exceeds the documented eight-byte maximum.
A numeric seven-digit Element 58 value is within the non-Amex width limit.
An eight-digit Element 58 value exceeds the seven-byte limit for non-Amex card types.

openQuestions: Confirm card-brand/card-type encoding for each Segment 100 fixture and how the Amex width exception is selected.
Confirm assumed decimal and currency context; these vectors test width/range only, not amount arithmetic.
Resolve whether the general 1-99999999 valid range is constrained by the non-Amex seven-byte representation in all card contexts.
Review full Segment 100 request fixtures and expected outcomes before execution or promotion.
